hyps.why: With the direct 0->3 edge removed, cutting 2->3 leaves only the 1->3 path, so the damage is much larger.
If 2->3 is already none, removing the 0->3 edge removes one of only two remaining routes to the output.
When 1->3 is none, the output depends heavily on 2->3, so removing it is especially harmful.
Node 1 reaches the output only through edges 2 and 4, so with edge 4 removed a better op on 0->1 helps less.
Node 2 feeds the output only via edge 5, so improving 0->2 is nearly useless when edge 5 is none.
If 0->1 is none, node 1 carries zero signal, so the op on 1->2 has almost no effect.
Replacing none restores an output path and adds a strong conv, a far larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Adding a residual connection where none existed improves gradient flow much more than swapping out a conv on that edge.
avg_pool_3x3 is among the weakest ops on output edges, so upgrading it to a 3x3 conv gains more than upgrading other ops.
Without the 0->3 edge, removing 1->3 leaves the output fed only by node 2, which greatly increases the accuracy drop.
